emergencyNumbers.description: All-in-one unified emergency response system across India for Police, Fire, and Ambulance.

emergencyNumbers.name: NDMA Disaster Helpline
emergencyNumbers.description: National Disaster Management Authority control room for disaster alerts, rescue reports, and relief.

emergencyNumbers.name: State Disaster Helpline (Toll-Free)
emergencyNumbers.description: State Emergency Operations Center (SEOC) for district-level response and coordination.

emergencyNumbers.name: Emergency Medical Ambulance
emergencyNumbers.description: Government emergency ambulance service with life support dispatch.

emergencyNumbers.name: Fire & Rescue Brigade
emergencyNumbers.description: Immediate fire hazard containment, structural collapse, and urban rescue teams.

emergencyNumbers.name: Women Helpline
emergencyNumbers.description: 24/7 emergency response and distress assistance for women in crisis.

emergencyNumbers.name: Childline
emergencyNumbers.description: 24/7 national emergency response service for children in need of protection.

districts.name: Puri
advice: Identify the nearest pucca Cyclone Shelter (ODRRP) in your ward or gram panchayat.
Trim tree branches near overhead power lines and reinforce weak tin or asbestos roofs.
Store at least 5 days of drinking water in sealed, elevated containers.
Move cattle and livestock to elevated community flood shelters upon coastal alert issuance.

districts.name: Balasore
advice: Monitor Subarnarekha and Budhabalanga river discharge levels during monsoon.
Keep emergency battery torches, portable radios, and dry rations pre-packed.
Never attempt to cross flooded causeways or breached embankments on foot or by vehicle.

districts.name: Sambalpur
advice: Stay indoors between 11:30 AM and 3:30 PM when daytime temperatures exceed 42°C.
Always carry oral rehydration salts (ORS), butter milk, or lemon water when stepping outside.
Pay attention to Hirakud Dam spillway siren alerts during intense upstream rainfall.

districts.name: Kullu
advice: Avoid pitching tents or staying in homestays located along the Beas river active flood plain.
Inspect slope retention walls and ensure surface stormwater runoff drains freely away from foundations.
Kullu lies in Seismic Zone V: keep an earthquake survival grab-bag with whistle, first-aid, and thermal foil blankets.

districts.name: Kangra
advice: Retrofit unreinforced masonry and avoid unauthorized vertical structural additions.
Practice the Drop, Cover, and Hold On maneuver with family members every quarter.
Avoid driving on mountain roads after continuous 24-hour rainfall spells.

districts.name: Shimla
advice: Equip wooden residential buildings with functional dry chemical ABC fire extinguishers.
Monitor retaining walls for diagonal cracks or soil sinking along hillside lanes.
Keep emergency heating alternatives safe from carbon monoxide buildup in winter.

districts.name: Mumbai Suburban
advice: Check BMC high-tide forecasts before commuting during heavy monsoon spells.
Never walk through inundated waters where electric feeder boxes or junction poles are submerged.
Know your building's primary and alternate fire evacuation staircase.

districts.name: Raigad
advice: Heed immediate evacuation orders for settlements located at foot of unstable Western Ghat hills.
Secure boats, fishing equipment, and exterior solar panels prior to Arabian Sea depression landfall.
Store prescription medicines in waterproof bags.

districts.name: Nagpur
advice: Avoid continuous direct sun exposure during peak May heatwave periods.
Wear white, breathable cotton clothing and cover head with a wet cloth if outdoor transit is required.
Clean rooftop terrace drains before pre-monsoon convective thunderstorms.

districts.name: Dhemaji
advice: Keep emergency country boats, life vests, or bamboo floats accessible near riverside dwellings.
Store dry rations, flattened rice (chira), molasses, and water purification chlorine tablets on elevated bamboo machans.
Strictly avoid drinking unfiltered floodwater; boil all water vigorously.

districts.name: Kamrup Metropolitan (Guwahati)
advice: Guwahati sits in Seismic Zone V: fasten heavy bookcases, refrigerators, and water geysers firmly to walls.
Do not settle on deforested hill slopes prone to sudden mudflows during monsoon squalls.
Clear neighborhood drain inlets of plastic garbage to mitigate localized artificial flooding.

districts.name: Churu
advice: Avoid strenuous agricultural or physical work between 12:00 PM and 4:00 PM during Loo wind spells.
Maintain shaded spaces and water troughs for cattle and domestic animals.
Treat symptoms of heat exhaustion (dizziness, nausea, excessive thirst) immediately with electrolyte solutions.

districts.name: Jodhpur
advice: Maintain domestic traditional rainwater harvesting (tankas) in clean condition.
Be aware of flash runoff in rocky low-lying city alleys during sudden short cloudbursts.
Use heavy blinds and khus curtains on west-facing windows.

districts.name: Wayanad
advice: Comply immediately with district red alert relocation orders in designated high-slope landslide corridors.
Watch for environmental warning cues: abrupt muddying of spring water or small hillside soil crevices.
Keep emergency contact numbers of local ward panchayat disaster committees saved on speed dial.

districts.name: Alappuzha
advice: Store essential documents and medicines on high shelves or waterproof bags during Kuttanad waterlogging.
Prepare for early transit to safe relief camps before boat routes become hazardous.
Disinfect open well drinking water with chlorine bleaches once flood water recedes.

districts.name: Chamoli
advice: Do not venture near Alaknanda, Dhauliganga, or Rishi Ganga riverbanks during cloudburst or glacial lake advisories.
Follow SDRF instructions immediately regarding highway traffic halts on the Badrinath route.
Have an emergency survival kit packed at all times in mountain dwellings.

districts.name: Dehradun
advice: Adhere to earthquake building codes for all private residential constructions.
Avoid driving through swollen seasonal rivulets (raos) around Doon valley during heavy monsoon spells.
Keep emergency household escape plans rehearsed.

districts.name: Kutch
advice: Kutch is situated in the highest Seismic Zone V: avoid heavy overhead terrace masonry and secure unanchored walls.
During cyclone threats, evacuate coastal salt-pan worker settlements and kachha dwellings early.
Store conservative water supplies and livestock fodder provisions.

districts.name: Surat
advice: Check Tapi river Ukai Dam water release updates before planning movement in low-lying riverside areas.
Industrial and textile godown operators must keep fire hydrants and dry chemical extinguishers certified.
Unplug electrical equipment and lift appliances from ground floor levels during inundation warnings.

districts.name: Madhubani
advice: Keep emergency grain reserves in elevated grain silos (kothis).
Keep contact numbers of NDRF/SDRF boat team commanders posted at the block office.
Do not build permanent heavy masonry without tie-bands in high seismicity zones.

districts.name: Patna
advice: Keep mobile phone and battery inverters charged during high Ganga river discharge warnings.
Avoid direct afternoon sun during severe summer heatwaves; drink sattu and aam panna.
Ensure household electrical switchboards are inspected for loose connections.

districts.name: Chennai
advice: Know your neighborhood's nearest GCC relief community center and boat staging point.
Move motor vehicles to elevated multi-level parking structures ahead of red-alert northeast monsoon rain.
Keep adequate food, candles, matches, and drinking water for at least 72 hours.

districts.name: The Nilgiris
advice: Avoid all unnecessary travel along ghat roads during active heavy rainfall warnings.
Clear debris and leaf-clogged gutters around hill dwellings to prevent soil saturation.
Follow municipal advisories regarding structural vulnerability of slope residences.

disasterGuides.name: Flood & Flash Flood
disasterGuides.description: Rapid inundation from excessive monsoon rain, river breach, or cloudburst.
before: Store clean water in sealed containers and pack a waterproof grab-bag with documents.
Identify high ground and community evacuation centers in your ward or panchayat.
Elevate critical electrical panels and unplug major appliances.
during: Never drive or walk through moving floodwater (6 inches of water can knock you down).
Disconnect cooking gas cylinders and turn off the main electrical breaker.
Stay tuned to local government radio or official SMS alerts on mobile.
after: Avoid downed power lines, standing water pools, and damaged electrical wiring.
Boil all drinking water thoroughly for at least 1 minute before consuming.
Photograph building damage before starting debris cleanup for disaster relief claims.

disasterGuides.name: Cyclone & Coastal Storm Surge
disasterGuides.description: Severe cyclonic storms carrying destructive winds exceeding 120 km/h and intense rainfall.
before: Trim tree branches near power lines and secure loose tin roofing sheets.
Board up or tape glass windows and secure external solar panels or water tanks.
Keep battery-powered radios, torches, and extra batteries fully ready.
during: Remain indoors in the strongest, central room of the building away from glass windows.
Do not leave shelter when the eye of the storm passes (winds will resume suddenly).
Keep mobile phones switched to battery-saver mode and preserve charge.
after: Wait for official 'all-clear' announcement from IMD or local authorities before leaving shelter.
Watch for venomous snakes displaced into homes by floodwaters.
Do not touch snapped electric cables hanging from poles or submerged in water.

disasterGuides.name: Earthquake
disasterGuides.description: Sudden violent shaking of the ground caused by movement along geological fault lines.
before: Secure heavy cupboards, mirrors, and ceiling fans to wall studs with brackets.
Identify safe interior drop spots (under heavy wooden tables or beside interior load-bearing walls).
Assemble an emergency kit with whistle, torch, basic first-aid, and work gloves.
during: DROP to the ground, take COVER under a sturdy table, and HOLD ON until tremors cease.
If in bed, stay there and protect your head and neck with a pillow.
Do not use elevators or run into narrow crowded stairwells during shaking.
after: Be prepared for dangerous aftershocks over the next 24 to 72 hours.
Check for gas leaks immediately; do not strike matches or turn on light switches if gas is smelled.
Use a whistle or tap rhythmically on pipes if trapped under debris to signal rescue teams.

disasterGuides.name: Heatwave & Extreme Temperature
disasterGuides.description: Prolonged periods of abnormal thermal stress exceeding 40°C in plains and 30°C in hills.
before: Block direct solar heat into living rooms using damp dark curtains, bamboo blinds, or white paint on roofs.
Stock up on Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS), electrolyte powders, and glucose.
Plan outdoor labor and errands strictly before 10:00 AM or after 5:00 PM.
during: Drink water frequently, even if you do not feel thirsty.
Never leave children, infants, or pets inside parked vehicles even for a few minutes.
Wear loose, light-colored cotton clothing and cover head with cloth or an umbrella.
after: Recognize heat stroke signs: High body temperature (>40°C), confusion, vomiting, or no sweating.
Move heatstroke victims to shade immediately, apply cold wet towels, and dial 108/112.

disasterGuides.name: Landslide & Mudflow
disasterGuides.description: Downward movement of rock, earth, or debris triggered by intense rainfall or earth tremors.
before: Learn historical landslide zones in your hill station or highway corridor.
Watch for telltale warning signs: cracks in exterior walls, tilting fence posts or telephone poles.
Ensure surface stormwater drains flow safely away from slopes and foundation walls.
during: Quickly evacuate downhill structures if unusual sounds like trees cracking or boulders rolling are heard.
If escape is impossible, curl into a tight ball and protect your head with your arms.
Never cross mountain roads when small rocks or muddy streams begin sliding over the asphalt.
after: Stay away from slide areas; secondary landslides frequently follow initial slope failures.
Check for injured or trapped persons without entering direct slide path.
Report broken utility lines to SDMA and PWD helpline personnel immediately.

disasterGuides.name: Urban & Domestic Fire
disasterGuides.description: Rapid fire spread in residential buildings, informal settlements, or commercial spaces.
before: Install and check smoke alarms and maintain at least one ABC dry powder fire extinguisher.
Map two emergency escape exits from every room in your home or flat.
Never overload multi-plug electrical extension boards or use damaged cords.
during: Crawl low under smoke towards the nearest fire exit (smoke and toxic fumes rise to the ceiling).
Feel doors with the back of your hand; if the knob or door feels hot, do not open it.
If your clothes catch fire: STOP, DROP to the ground, and ROLL repeatedly.
after: Do not re-enter a burned building until cleared by the local fire brigade officer.
Cool minor burns with clean, cool running water for 10-15 minutes; never apply butter or grease.
Call 101 or 112 immediately if anyone requires medical or smoke inhalation care.
